record.final_answer:
No. The report doesn't measure the setup we'd be running, so it can't tell us whether the agents keep up at peak with TLS on.

**What the report measured** (Marrowlog 2.4, published 2026-06-18): one agent on 1 vCPU shipped 180,000 lines/s at 85% CPU. Those runs used:
- **No TLS at all.** Every run used plain TCP, and TLS is listed under "Not covered."
- **Lines of 200 bytes or less.**
- Disk buffer off and `batch_lines: 500`, which matches our `config/agent.yaml`.

**Our peak** (from `README.md`): 50,000 lines/s per agent at about 900 bytes per line, on 1 vCPU.

**Why it doesn't carry over:**
- **TLS isn't measured.** Encryption costs CPU, and their run was already at 85% CPU without it, so there's little headroom left.
- **It isn't even clear we keep up today.** 180,000 lines/s at 200 bytes or less is at most about 36 MB/s. Our peak is about 45 MB/s (50k × 900 B), which is more than they measured even over plain TCP. Our line count is lower than theirs, but per-byte work like JSON parsing and compression grows with line size. TLS cost also scales with bytes, which makes this the number that matters.

**What I'd do:**
1. Run our own load test: one agent on 1 vCPU, `tls: true`, replaying real logs (or about 900-byte JSON lines) at 50k lines/s for at least 30 minutes. Watch CPU, lag on the tailed files, and whether anything is dropped.
2. Run the same test with `tls: false` as a baseline. That will also show whether we have headroom today.
3. The maintainers say TLS will be in their Q4 report. That can back up our test but probably won't replace it, since our lines are 4–5× longer than theirs.

I saved a note in memcue that this report covers only plain TCP with short lines, so a later session won't rely on it for the TLS decision.
